{"skill":"# Temporal contract skill: admission, ownership, and effect validity

Purpose: complete the original maintenance task. Use this skill to inspect timing and ownership where relevant; it adds no product requirements and does not replace implementation or verification.

S1 Applicability. Check whether an input or operation can complete after its initiating access, attempt, or consumer changes; whether callbacks can change ownership during a call; or whether one result feeds effects with different lifetimes. If none applies, briefly record the source basis and continue the maintenance task.

S2 Establish evidence. Inspect the entry point, producer or decoder, registration and removal, completion path, ownership transitions, cancellation, and every affected consumer. Inspect the actual dependency behavior where available. Cite source locations. Keep task requirements, observed source facts, hypotheses, and unavailable evidence distinct. Do not derive guarantees from names, plausible formats, or a failed check alone.

S3 Trace input admission separately from completion. For each relevant event, identify when reception becomes possible, when an input is accepted for work, when reception is retired, and whether accepted work can finish afterward. Check whether removal commits before a callback and whether that callback can synchronously reenter selection, cancellation, or cleanup. A post-transition input newly received by a retired operation has a different contract from an earlier accepted input that settles later. Establish the distinction from the project before deciding whether either effect should occur.

S4 Map identities and effects. Distinguish resource, access or visit, physical operation or attempt, and accepted input or result when the code does. Track where each identity is captured, replaced, and compared. For every effect, state its independent validity rule from task and source evidence: for example, a durable record may follow accepted work while a current view may require current ownership and result order. Determine whether cancellation stops future reception, aborts accepted work, or only retires a consumer. Do not apply one validity guard to all effects.

S5 Compare concrete orders. Use visible, controllable APIs to exercise ordinary startup and streaming; a transition before a new input; a transition after input acceptance but before completion; reuse of the same resource; replacement or retry when present; and synchronous callback reentry where supported. Observe durable and current effects separately. For ordered full results, test both normal and reversed completion order and identify the ordering key from source evidence. Avoid inventing data schemas or assuming that completion order equals input order.

S6 Preserve adjacent contracts. Check existing public shapes, notifications, cancellation, cleanup, and other consumers of shared helpers where the change can affect them. Background obligations, rollback, permission withdrawal, or dependencies that suppress completion can alter the contract; verify these in visible code or leave them unresolved. Do not generalize persistence after cancellation or access-based suppression across projects.

S7 Repair and verify. Make the smallest source-supported change that completes the original task, or explain with evidence why no change is needed or why completion remains blocked. Run relevant available checks and inspect their actual output. Add focused checks for uncovered event orders, especially the distinction between newly admitted post-transition input and previously accepted late completion. Revise when evidence contradicts the proposed contract. A passing local harness establishes only the paths it drives; assess whole-task behavior separately and report failed or unrun checks. Preserve the maintenance objective through the final deliverable.","change_notes":[{"step":"Admission","change":"Added an explicit boundary between new input after retirement and earlier accepted work settling later.","feedback_basis":"The scored difference was an extra history entry from a newly emitted input after navigation; accepted late work remained valid on observed paths."},{"step":"Ordering","change":"Require transition-before-input and input-before-transition comparisons, including reentrant callbacks.","feedback_basis":"The local harness covered stale completion and several lifecycle paths but did not establish the reported input-admission boundary."},{"step":"Validation","change":"Limit conclusions from local checks and distinguish whole-task behavior from selected passes.","feedback_basis":"Local checks passed while the whole behavior score was 0.0; the trace did not uniquely establish a cause."}]}
